title: harness capability manifest document
description: Canonical form of a harness capability manifest: the capability set one harness node provides to a CodegenBundle, under a versioned ABI. No person writes it: the host derives the set from the target profile that names the harness (tools/target_profile.py:harness_capabilities, issue #690), renders it in this document form (tools/codegen_bundle.py:harness_capability_manifest_document_for) and validates the shape with harness_capability_manifest_violations. Negotiation matches an exact name@version token: version ordering never implies compatibility, and a harness that does not resolve fails the run closed.

harness_capability_abi_version.description: The ABI generation this manifest document is written against. Pinned, not a floor: this contract is generation HARNESS_CAPABILITY_ABI_VERSION = 1, and a later-generation manifest is rejected rather than read under generation-1 semantics (forward compatibility is never assumed — the same rule the exact name@version token match applies to a single capability).

manifests.description: One entry per harness node_key; the host renders one, for the target's harness. An absent node_key provides nothing.

node_key.description: The harness node this manifest describes. Only an infrastructure node provides capabilities.

provides.description: The capability tokens this harness provides, duplicate-free. sync_single_case@1 is the synchronous single-case block the target language's backend pins (assert_harness_pin) under the providing harness node's own names: the operations and the published type the host-rendered runner calls, dp = float64, case_id_len = 64; every target provides it. distributed_state@2 is the distributed-state block the language backend pins after it (rank queries, the process grid the host imposes and its queries, block partition and halo exchange along one grid dimension, gather onto rank 0 of an array partitioned along up to two grid dimensions with its tile check, global reductions), with the writers called on rank 0 only; a target whose parallel backend declares a launcher provides it. capture_format_<id>@1 names the output format the harness's capture operations write, <id> the target profile's output.format; no bundle requires it.

capability_token.description: <capability_name>@<abi_version>. The name must be a member of the closed vocabulary below; the version is an exact integer, never a range.

x-forbidden-examples.note: a capability name outside the closed vocabulary
a version range; only an exact integer version is a token
a bare name with no ABI version
only an infrastructure node provides capabilities

x-forbidden-examples-note: This schema rejects on its own: a version range and a bare name (the token pattern), and a non-infrastructure node_key (the node_key pattern). A well-formed token whose NAME is outside x-capability-vocabulary (gpu_magic@1) matches the token pattern and is rejected by the canonical validator, tools/codegen_bundle.py:harness_capability_manifest_violations, which holds the vocabulary as a closed set.
